o: Where did you go last summer?
Where did you went last summer?
R1.e: Past simple questions: question word + did + subject + base verb. So: Where did you go?
We say take a photo / take a selfie, not make or do.

R1.q: My brother is very ___. He always tells jokes and makes us laugh.
R1.e: A funny person makes other people laugh. Shy and quiet people don't talk much.

R1.q: Look! Marco ___ his new jacket today.
R1.e: Look! and today show something happening now, so we use the present continuous: is + -ing.

R1.q: The cat is sleeping ___ the sofa and the chair.
R1.e: Between = in the middle of two things. We say next to and in front of, with to / of.

R1.q: Last summer we ___ to Greece by ferry.
R1.e: Go is irregular. The past simple is went. Gone is the past participle.

R1.q: We ___ camping in the mountains for a week.
R1.e: We say go camping (past: went camping). Also go swimming, go sightseeing.

R1.q: I ___ a shower when the phone rang.
R1.e: Past continuous (was/were + -ing) for an action in progress when something else happened. I + was.

R1.q: We went to the beach. ___, it started to rain, so we went home.
R1.e: Suddenly = quickly and unexpectedly. We use it to tell a story. The other words join two clauses.

R1.q: You can't remember the word 'shy'. Which is the best way to explain it?
R1.e: When you don't know a word, you can paraphrase: It's the opposite of..., It's a kind of..., It's something you...

R1.q: Look at those black clouds! It ___ (rain – be going to).
R1.e: We use be going to for a prediction when we can see evidence now, like black clouds.

R1.q: Before you get on the plane, you wait in the departure l___.
R1.e: The departure lounge is the area at the airport where passengers wait for their flight.

R1.q: We ___ (have) dinner with our grandparents on Sunday. It's all arranged.
R1.e: Present continuous for future arrangements: we are + -ing.
The verb wait always takes for before a person or thing: wait for someone.

R1.q: A chef is a person ___ cooks in a restaurant.
R1.e: In defining relative clauses we use who (or that) for people.

R2.q: Have you replied to Marta's message ___?
R2.e: Yet is used in questions and negatives with the present perfect. It goes at the end of the sentence.
We say do the washing-up, do the ironing, do the housework.
Last year is a finished time, so we use the past simple, not the present perfect.

R2.q: If you want to try on clothes in a shop, you go to the ___.
R2.e: The changing rooms are where you try clothes on. You pay at the checkout.

R2.q: I'm hungry but there isn't ___ in the fridge.
R2.e: In negative sentences we use anything. Nothing already has a negative meaning, so we don't use it with isn't.

R2.q: The film was really ___. I nearly fell asleep.
R2.e: Adjectives with -ing describe the thing (a boring film). -ed adjectives describe how people feel.
To compare how people do things we use comparative adverbs: more + adverb (carefully).

R2.q: It's the best pizza I've ___ eaten.
R2.e: Superlative + present perfect + ever: the best... I've ever eaten.

R2.q: I can't buy it. I haven't got ___ money.
R2.e: Enough goes before a noun: enough money = the amount you need. Money is uncountable, so not many / too many.

R2.q: It's cold in here. ___ I close the window?
R2.e: We use Shall I...? to offer to do something for someone.

R2.q: I've got a sore t___, so I can't speak very well.
R2.e: Your throat is inside your neck. If it hurts, it's difficult to speak.
In English we use a point (.) in decimals, not a comma: four point five.

R2.q: I think it ___ (not / be) very hot tomorrow.
R2.e: For predictions we use will / won't + base verb. Won't = will not.
Win and lose are opposite verbs: win a match / lose a match.

R2.q: I'm busy now. I'll call you ___ later.
R2.e: Call someone back = phone them again, usually after they called you.

R3.q: I went to the chemist's ___ some medicine.
R3.e: We use to + infinitive to say why we do something: I went there to buy...
Decide is followed by to + infinitive: decide to do something.
We use the gerund (-ing) as the subject of a sentence: Swimming is good...
Mind is followed by the gerund (-ing): Do you mind closing...?

R3.q: You ___ wear a uniform at my school. It's optional.
R3.e: Don't have to = it isn't necessary. Mustn't = it is not allowed.
We say afraid of / terrified of / scared of something.

R3.q: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.
R3.e: Should + base verb (no to) to give advice. Ought needs to: ought to.

R3.q: If the sea ___ calm on Saturday, we'll go sailing.
R3.e: First conditional: if + present simple, will + verb. No will after if.
Possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his...) replace a noun. Yours never has an apostrophe.

R3.q: If I ___ a lot of money, I'd buy a house by the sea.
R3.e: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + verb. It's an imaginary situation.

R3.q: What time do you usually get ___ in the morning?
R3.e: Get up = leave your bed after sleeping.
The adverb from good is well (irregular). It describes how she speaks.

R3.q: My parents have had this car ___ 2019.
R3.e: Since + a point in time (2019). For + a period of time (ten years).

R3.q: A b___ is an insect that makes honey.
R3.e: Bees are insects that make honey. They can sting you.
In 2010 is a finished time, so we use the past simple. Win → won (irregular).

R4.q: The ball went ___ the window and broke the glass.
R4.e: Through = in one side and out of the other: the ball went through the window.

R4.q: In football, the ___ makes sure the players follow the rules.
R4.e: The referee controls the match. The coach trains the team.

R4.q: Your coat's on the floor. Please ___.
R4.e: With a pronoun (it, them), it goes between the verb and the particle: pick it up.

R4.q: The first pizza margherita ___ in Naples.
R4.e: Past passive: was/were + past participle (made). The pizza didn't make itself!
People from Switzerland are Swiss. Swedish people come from Sweden.

R4.q: I ___ like vegetables, but now I love them.
R4.e: Negative of used to: didn't use to + verb (no -d after didn't).

R4.q: Don't wait for me. I ___ be late tonight.
R4.e: Might + base verb = maybe it will happen. No to, no -s.

R4.q: 'I can't stand cold weather.' '___ can I.'
R4.e: To agree with a negative sentence we use Neither + auxiliary + I: Neither can I. So is for positive sentences.

R4.q: When we got to the station, the train ___.
R4.e: Past perfect (had + past participle) for an action that happened before another past action.

R4.q: She ___ me that she was tired.
R4.e: Tell + person: she told me. Say has no person after it: she said that...

R4.q: In h___ lessons you learn about the past.
R4.e: History is the school subject about events in the past.
Many verbs make nouns with -ion / -sion: decide → decision.

R4.q: 'I'm hungry.' → Yesterday Luca said he ___ hungry.
R4.e: In reported speech the present usually moves back to the past: am → was.
When who is the subject, we don't use did: Who wrote...?

R4.q: Please turn ___ your phones before the lesson starts.
R4.e: Turn off = stop a machine or light working. The opposite is turn on.

T1.q: Which question is correct?
o: What kind of music you like?
What kind of music like you?
What kind music do you like?
What kind of music do you like?
T1.e: Present simple questions: question word(s) + do/does + subject + verb. And we say kind of music.

T1.q: My sister ___ coffee. She hates it.
T1.e: Present simple negative with he/she/it: doesn't + base verb (no -s).

T1.q: I usually ___ to school, but today I'm getting the bus.
T1.e: Usually = a habit, so we use the present simple. Today (now) uses the present continuous.

T1.q: She's very ___. She never gives anything to anyone.
T1.e: A mean person doesn't like giving or sharing things. Generous is the opposite.

T1.q: It's freezing today. Put on your ___ before you go out.
T1.e: When it's very cold you wear a coat. Sandals, shorts and swimsuits are for hot weather.

T1.q: We ___ the film because it was too long.
T1.e: Past simple negative: didn't + base verb. The verb doesn't change after didn't.

T1.q: The beach was very ___. There were hundreds of people.
T1.e: Crowded = full of people. Empty, peaceful and quiet mean there aren't many people.

T1.q: What ___ you doing at eight o'clock last night?
T1.e: Past continuous question: was/were + subject + -ing. With you we use were.

T1.q: The accident happened ___ I was driving home.
T1.e: While + subject + verb (usually past continuous). During is followed by a noun: during the night.

T1.q: I love walking along the beach ___ night.
T1.e: We say at night, but in the morning / in the evening.

T1.q: I was very tired, ___ I went to bed early.
T1.e: So introduces a result: I was tired → result: I went to bed early.

T1.q: Be careful! You ___ fall!
T1.e: Be going to + verb for a prediction based on what we can see now.

T1.q: That's the café ___ we had breakfast yesterday.
T1.e: We use where in relative clauses for places: the café where we had breakfast.

T1.q: After the flight, you collect your suitcases at ___.
T1.e: Baggage reclaim is where you collect your bags after you land.

T1.q: I ___ (not / go) out last night. I stayed at home.
T1.e: Past simple negative: didn't + base verb: didn't go.

T1.q: She ___ (read) a book when I arrived.
T1.e: Past continuous (was + -ing) for an action in progress when another action happened.

T1.q: I don't know if we can go. It depends ___ the weather.
T1.e: The verb depend always takes on: it depends on...

T1.q: We ___ (visit) my aunt in Rome next month. We've already decided.
T1.e: For future plans we use be going to + verb (or the present continuous for arrangements).

T1.q: Your plane is boarding now. Please go to g___ 12.
T1.e: At the airport, the gate is where you get on the plane.

T1.q: The boy ___ lives next door is my cousin.
T1.e: Who (or that) introduces a relative clause about a person.

T2.q: I've ___ seen that film. Let's watch something else.
T2.e: Already = before now, sooner than expected. It goes between have and the past participle.

T2.q: 'Where's Anna?' 'She's ___ gone out. You missed her by two minutes.'
T2.e: Just = a very short time ago. It goes between have/has and the past participle.

T2.q: Try not to ___ so many mistakes in your homework.
T2.e: We say make a mistake, make a noise, make a phone call.

T2.q: When ___ your new phone?
T2.e: Questions with When ask about a finished time in the past, so we use the past simple.

T2.q: When you pay, the shop assistant gives you a ___.
T2.e: A receipt is the piece of paper that shows what you bought and how much you paid.

T2.q: Is there ___ who can help me?
T2.e: In questions we often use anybody/anyone for people. Anything is for things; anywhere and somewhere are for places.

T2.q: I was ___ when I heard the news.
T2.e: -ed adjectives describe how a person feels: I was shocked. The news was shocking.

T2.q: My flat isn't as big ___ yours.
T2.e: (not) as + adjective + as to compare two things: not as big as.

T2.q: It's the ___ place I've ever visited.
T2.e: Long adjectives form the superlative with the most: the most beautiful.

T2.q: There's a beautiful old ___ in the city centre. People go there to pray.
T2.e: A cathedral is a large, important church where people pray. A town hall is for the local government.

T2.q: There are ___ people here. I can't move!
T2.e: Too many + plural countable noun (people). Too much is for uncountable nouns.

T2.q: 'The phone's ringing.' 'I ___ answer it.'
T2.e: We use will ('ll) for decisions we make at the moment of speaking, and for offers.

T2.q: The exam was ___ difficult. Nobody finished it.
T2.e: Incredibly = extremely. Nobody finished, so it was very, very difficult.

T2.q: I ___ in a bank at the moment, but I want to change jobs.
T2.e: At the moment → present continuous: am + -ing (I'm working).

T2.q: I haven't finished my project ___.
T2.e: Yet goes at the end of negative sentences with the present perfect: I haven't... yet.

T2.q: You use your t___ to taste food.
T2.e: Your tongue is in your mouth. You use it to taste and to speak.

T2.q: Don't worry, you ___ (pass) the exam. You've studied a lot.
T2.e: Will + base verb for a prediction about the future (be going to is also possible here).

T2.q: The opposite of 'remember' is f___.
T2.e: Remember and forget are opposite verbs.

T2.q: If the shoes are too small, you can take them ___ to the shop.
T2.e: Take something back = return it to the place where you got it.

T2.q: I ___ (never / be) to Venice.
T2.e: Present perfect for experiences: have + never + past participle (been).

T3.q: It's difficult ___ when my neighbours are so noisy.
T3.e: After It's + adjective we use to + infinitive: It's difficult to sleep...

T3.q: I forgot ___ my mum, so she was worried.
T3.e: Forget to do something = not remember to do something you needed to do.

T3.q: I'm really looking forward ___ you.
T3.e: Look forward to + -ing. Here to is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.

T3.q: You ___ use your phone during the exam. It's against the rules.
T3.e: Mustn't = it is not allowed. Don't have to = it isn't necessary.

T3.q: I'm not very interested ___ politics.
T3.e: We say interested in something.

T3.q: It's getting ___. Let's go home.
T3.e: Get + adjective = become: it's getting dark, cold, late.

T3.q: Do you think I ___ tell her the truth?
T3.e: Should + base verb. It never changes (no -s) and has no to after it.

T3.q: If you don't hurry, you ___ the bus.
T3.e: First conditional: if + present simple, will ('ll) + verb for a likely result.

T3.q: Can I ___ your pen, please?
T3.e: Borrow = take something for a short time. Lend = give it for a short time.

T3.q: That's not my phone. ___ is black.
T3.e: Mine = my phone. A possessive pronoun can be the subject without a noun.

T3.q: He drove very ___ and had an accident.
T3.e: Adverbs of manner (-ly) describe how someone does something: drive dangerously. Dangerous is an adjective.

T3.q: What would you do if you ___ a snake in your garden?
T3.e: Second conditional: if + past simple (saw), would + verb.

T3.q: Giulia has played the piano ___ six months.
T3.e: For + a period of time: for six months. Since + a point in time.

T3.q: Leonardo da Vinci ___ many famous paintings.
T3.e: He is dead, so his life is finished: we use the past simple.

T3.q: Horror films t___ me (= make me very afraid). I can't watch them.
T3.e: Terrify = make someone very, very afraid.

T3.q: If I ___ (be) you, I'd take the job.
T3.e: Second conditional to give advice: If I were you... (was is also possible).

T3.q: An insect with beautiful coloured wings is a b___.
T3.e: A butterfly is an insect with large, colourful wings.

T3.q: She was b___ in Palermo in 1990.
T3.e: In biographies we say was/were born + place + year.

T3.q: You ___ (not / have to) come if you don't want to.
T3.e: Don't have to = it isn't necessary. You can choose.

T3.q: I don't mind ___ (wait).
T3.e: Mind is followed by a verb in the -ing form: I don't mind waiting.

T4.q: The children ran ___ the hill to the top.
T4.e: Up = from a lower place to a higher place. They went to the top.

T4.q: Our team ___ the match 3–1.
T4.e: Win a match / game. Beat a team or person: we beat them 3–1.

T4.q: I don't know this word. I'll ___.
T4.e: Look up = find in a dictionary. The pronoun goes in the middle: look it up.

T4.q: English ___ in many countries.
T4.e: Present passive: is/are + past participle. The subject (English) doesn't do the action.

T4.q: My friend comes from Portugal. She's ___.
T4.e: People from Portugal are Portuguese. Countries and nationalities often have different words.

T4.q: ___ you use to play with dolls when you were little?
T4.e: Questions with used to: Did + subject + use to + verb?

T4.q: I'm not sure. I ___ go to the party.
T4.e: Might = maybe. We use it when we are not sure.

T4.q: 'I've been to Paris.' 'So ___ I.'
T4.e: In So... I we repeat the auxiliary from the first sentence: I've been → So have I.

T4.q: My sister and I are very ___. We both love music and sport.
T4.e: Similar = almost the same. We say the same, not very same.

T4.q: I didn't watch the film because I ___ it before.
T4.e: Past perfect (had + past participle) for something that happened earlier than another past action.

T4.q: 'I will call you.' → She said she ___ call me.
T4.e: In reported speech will changes to would.

T4.q: Can you ___ me the time, please?
T4.e: We say tell someone something: tell me the time.

T4.q: Who ___ you this present?
T4.e: Who is the subject of the question, so we don't use did: Who gave you...?

T4.q: I'd never been there ___.
T4.e: Before = at an earlier time. Ago always needs a time period: two years ago.

T4.q: '___ does this word mean?' 'It means very tired.'
T4.e: We ask What does... mean? to ask the meaning of a word.

T4.q: The study of numbers at school: m___
T4.e: Maths (short for mathematics) is the subject about numbers.

T4.q: The ___ (discover) of penicillin changed medicine.
T4.e: The noun from discover is discovery.

T4.q: Your shoes are dirty. Please take ___ (them / off).
T4.e: With a pronoun, the order is verb + pronoun + particle: take them off.

T4.q: This church ___ (build) in the 17th century.
T4.e: Past passive: was + past participle (built).

T4.q: 'I can swim.' → Last summer he said he ___ swim.
T4.e: In reported speech can changes to could.
